I've written the plan as separate sessions, as you asked. One session could build this, so the split mainly costs extra start-up time; `plan.md` notes it was split on request. No piece has been started yet.

| Wave | Piece | Model | Effort | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 01 skeleton + db | opus | medium | Sets the schema and function signatures every later piece builds on |
| 2 | 02 importers | sonnet | medium | Handles money parsing, all-or-nothing imports and duplicate skipping; the spec is clear and tests will catch mistakes |
| 2 | 03 rules | sonnet | medium | Clear priority and tie-break rules, easy to test |
| 2 | 04 budgets | sonnet | medium | Simple totals, easy to test |
| 3 | 05 cli | sonnet | medium | Connects the existing functions to commands; tests check the output format |
| 3 | final review | opus | medium | Required because the code handles money |

Wave 1 fixes the database schema before anything else is built. Transactions get a `category_source` column (empty, `'rule'` or `'manual'`), so recategorizing can never overwrite a category you set by hand. Each piece in wave 2 owns only its own module and test file, so those three can run in parallel in separate worktrees. Only wave 1 has a full prompt; the wave 2 and 3 prompts get written once wave 1 is done, so they match the code that actually exists.

Files are in `.brigade/`:
- `context.md`: the project map and the agreed interfaces
- `plan.md`: the waves, how to run them, and your full spec copied word for word
- `prompts/01-skeleton-db.md`: the prompt for piece 01
- `progress.md`: empty; each session adds its report here

Start the first piece with:

    claude --model opus --effort medium "Do brigade piece 01: follow .brigade/prompts/01-skeleton-db.md"

In VS Code or the desktop app, open a new chat, pick Opus, and send the same sentence. When piece 01 is done, run `/brigade next` to get the wave 2 prompts.
